rationale: Reference class: AAA games with an official date about 6 weeks out and active marketing; base rate about 0.88 (general knowledge, not a counted sample). Evidence: Rockstar's newswire and Xbox pages confirm Nov 19, 2026 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S; coverage dated early Nov treats it as firm, with a launch trailer out recently and pre-load reportedly from Nov 12. Raised a few points within the 15-point band. Strongest argument against: GTA 6 has already slipped twice (fall 2025, then May 26, 2026), and leaks are circulating.

Reference class: NASA eclipse livestreams. Base rate about 0.30 (1 of 2 known cases). Described benchmarks: 2024 peak 1,458,212; 2017 reported 2-3 million. Search found no official NASA peak figure for the Aug 12, 2026 stream. One guide claimed 15M+ for 2024, which conflicts with NASA's own figure, so I discarded it. The path lay mostly outside the US, which the description says may lower viewing. Lowered slightly because no official number has surfaced and NASA may not publish one by Nov 12.

Reference class: established mainstream software products still in service days after a question is asked; base rate about 0.97-0.99 (no shutdown of a major suite in a comparable window). No search needed. Description is empty, so the question is read as plain continued availability. Small residual for ambiguity in what counts as 'active'.

Reference class: large private tech companies listing on a US exchange within a specific two-week window; base rate about 0.03 (rare without a public filing). Evidence raises it: Anthropic publicly filed its S-1 on Oct 26, 2026 and applied for Nasdaq ticker ANT. Press reports point to a November listing, and the roadshow cannot begin before Nov 10 under the 15-day rule. No pricing date or first trading day has been announced, and the Amendment No. 1 report rests on one source. Moved up within the band but not to the level of a set date.

Reference class: new voluntary pledges that a specific large country signs at a given COP; base rate about 0.15 (my judgment, not a counted sample). The 35-by-35 pledge is a COP31 presidency target to raise electricity to 35% of final energy by 2035, launched in New York. The US formally withdrew from the agreement and will not send an official delegation. One outlet reports India refused to sign, but that rests on a single source. No information found on China. Lowered from base.

Reference class: nuclear weapon use in armed conflict; base rate effectively 0 (no use since 1945, about 80 years, 0 cases). Search found only a Tucker Carlson claim that the White House disputed and that the sources call unverified. Trump has said conventional options suffice and ruled out a nuclear bomb. CNN reported that plans for Pickaxe include a MOAB, which is conventional. Kept at the 0.01 floor, not moved above base.

Reference class: EU tax directive revisions adopted at a specific ECOFIN meeting; base rate about 0.10 (these need unanimity and this revision has stalled). Evidence: the Council Presidency put a compromise on the table for this Nov 9 meeting and says the pouch rate must be resolved there, which is specific evidence. The draft text covers e-cigarette liquids and nicotine pouches. Open issues remain (Swedish and Spanish reservations; the pouch minimum). Raised to the top of the 15-point band. Strongest argument against: the meeting may end without a deal, as other tax files have.

Same event and evidence as mf:dLEZL5CLgc. Reference class: large private companies listing on a US exchange in a specific two-week window; base rate about 0.03. S-1 publicly filed Oct 26, 2026, ticker ANT applied for on Nasdaq, and press reports point to November listing with a roadshow no earlier than Nov 10. No pricing date announced. Resolution needs shares listed and open for trading by Nov 20.

Reference class: codenamed Google models released to the general public within a specific one-week window after a leak report; base rate about 0.07 (judgment, not a counted sample). Reports say Google announced Carbon on Oct 28 for a limited group of cyber defenders, with no public date. I could not confirm that announcement against a Google primary source. Qualifying requires general public access, not closed or partial access. Lowered slightly from base.

Same event and evidence as mf:gPA98L9uQS. Reference class and base rate: AAA games with official dates about 6 weeks out; about 0.88. This version resolves YES on any release on or before Nov 19, so early release also counts. Rockstar and Xbox pages confirm Nov 19, 2026 and recent coverage treats it as firm. Strongest argument against: two prior delays.

Reference class: formal US announcements ending a blockade or sanctions regime within a short window; base rate about 0.10 (judgment). The blockade was reinstated July 13-14, 2026 and is still in place as of early Nov. Evidence raises it somewhat: Trump says a decision on strikes, a deal, or continued pressure is coming 'soon', and Qatar and Pakistan are working on an interim arrangement that would end the blockade of ports. Advisers are split (Rubio, Bessent and Ratcliffe favor keeping it). The question requires a clear, general, official end announcement, so partial or conditional statements do not count.

Reference class: a predicted recurrent nova not erupting in a given few-day window; base rate about 0.02 for a window of four days. Search found no outburst as of early Nov 2026. A catalog reading from Nov 4 gives V about 9.8, close to quiescence (about 10). The only open prediction is Feb 8, 2027 +/- 8 days, and the June 2026 date has passed without an eruption. Reaching mag 5 is far brighter than the 1866 (mag 2) and 1946 (mag 3) outbursts, so the chance is lower still. Held at the floor.
